text:
Support Eng - Lia: FYI customer AcmeSearch reporting indexing failures after yesterday's embed model swap. Their backfill keeps failing with a vector-shape error and we're seeing spikes of 429s on the embeddings endpoint. stack trace snippet below. :rotating_light:

Maya R: can you paste the exact error and the model id they hit? Was there a model version swap in prod?

Support Eng - Lia: error in indexer logs -> "ERROR Indexer: Unsupported vector shape: expected 1536, received 768". Customer payload sample attached and reproduction curl below. They say it started right after we switched their account to new model id.

Aj Chen: I rolled a config change yesterday at 2025-11-06T22:14Z that updated default embedding model for the account mapping. deploy: https://ci/redwood/deploys/abc123 (sha abc123). New model returns 768-d vectors; old one was 1536. We didn't coordinate a reindex.

Support Eng - Lia: reproduction curl (token redacted):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-slim-v1","input":["hello","world"]}'
```
Response shows embeddings length 768.

Ingest Runner Bot: indexer-job-3487 failed: vector_size_mismatch; retry 2/5. Last error: "Index validation failed: expected 1536 got 768"

Sandeep Patel: Indexer currently enforces a fixed vector dimension because the downstream vector index (faiss) was built for 1536. Options:
- quick mitigation: pad inbound 768 vectors with zeros to 1536 (cheap, preserves search shape but changes similarity semantics)
- prefered: schedule an index rebuild on the DB side to accept 768 (expensive, reindex time depends on corpus size)
I'll need to know corpus size and whether customers want old semantics kept.

DB Ops: Confirmed: the existing vector index was built with dimension=1536. Rebuild steps (one-off):
```
-- example for pgvector (psql)
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE items DROP INDEX IF EXISTS items_vector_idx;
CREATE INDEX items_vector_idx ON items USING ivfflat (embedding VECTOR(768)) WITH (lists = 100);
COMMIT;
```
That will require a maintenance window and full reindex. Alternative is to keep index as-is and transform vectors at ingest.

Aj Chen: another contributing factor: our batch size defaults to 128 for the embed-to-index pipeline. When large requests come in, we sometimes exceed our per-request token budget and the embeddings API returns partial successes which the indexer doesn't handle gracefully. Recommend lowering batch_size to 64 and enabling per-item retry/failover.

Support Eng - Lia: adding a minimal Python repro (customer-provided):
```
from requests import post
r = post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED'}, json={'model':'open-embed-slim-v1','input':['a'*10]})
print(len(r.json()['data'][0]['embedding']))  # -> 768
```
Then attempt to push to indexer via our ingest endpoint and you'll see validation error.

AcmeOps: we did indeed switch our model mapping to the smaller model last night via the console. We didn't realize the downstream index was fixed-dim. We need a stopgap so search doesn't break for customers. Timeline?

Sandeep Patel: Proposed action plan (short -> long):
1) Hotfix (0-2h): indexer accepts 768 by automatically upconverting by padding zeros to 1536. Implement in indexer worker and ship canary to a small subset of customers. (owner: Sandeep)
2) Medium (2-12h): run a backfill job that converts existing 1536 vectors to 768 semantics if customer opts in, or rebuild index to match 768. DB Ops to coordinate maintenance window. (owner: DB Ops + Ingest)
3) Long (>12h): add model-dim-awareness to onboarding + console warnings + block mismatched model assignments when index exists. (owner: Aj)

Support Eng - Lia: I'll communicate the hotfix plan + advise AcmeSearch to pin their account to the old model if they want original similarity behavior. Also asking them whether they'd prefer rebuild vs padded vectors. Marking this P0 for AcmeSearch until we confirm.

Ingest Runner Bot: queued backfill job backfill-20260315-001 for AcmeSearch. ETA: 04:00:00 (wall).

Maya R: also check auth/scopes — if the embed requests were proxied through a service account with different quotas we could be hitting rate-limits causing partial responses (see 429 spikes). Quick check: customer quota usage spiked at 22:12Z. @Aj can you confirm rate limiting logs?

Aj Chen: pulling rate-limit logs now. I see burst at 22:12Z for that org, we had a short-lived 429 cascade from quota-checker when batch retries piled up. We'll patch quota-checker to be more lenient for backfills and surface per-request failure counts in the console.

Support Eng - Lia: Next steps summary (owners):
- Sandeep: implement padding hotfix and canary (1.5h)
- DB Ops: prep reindex plan and estimate (3h)
- Aj: reduce default batching and adjust quota-checker (2h)
- Lia: notify AcmeSearch and collect preference for rebuild vs padding (30m)
Please update this thread as you make progress. :pray:
